facts.text: South Lansing is part of the Town of Lansing, named after New York jurist John Lansing Jr., the state chancellor.
South Lansing was part of the Town of Genoa in Cayuga County before becoming a separate town in 1817 when Tompkins County was created.
Before European settlement, the South Lansing area was part of the Cayuga Nation's territory, used for hunting, fishing, and agriculture.
South Lansing sits on the eastern shore of Cayuga Lake, with rolling uplands rising from the lake and steep gorges carved by Salmon Creek.
The Cayuga Shores Wildlife Management Area, a 287‑acre preserve along 3,400 feet of lakeshore, protects water quality and biodiversity in South Lansing.
South Lansing lies about five miles north of Ithaca, placing it within easy reach of Cornell University and the broader Ithaca community.
